document_title: Redwood Private Upgrade and Rollback Procedure Guidance
document_summary: Defines the supported upgrade paths, rollback procedures, and required service level agreements for Redwood Private instances.
supported_paths: Major version skipping requires prior technical review
prerequisites_for_rollback: Pre-upgrade backup/snapshot of control-plane database must exist
Pre-upgrade backup/snapshot of configuration state must exist
Upgrade must not cross a non-reversible schema boundary
rollback_process: Stop/roll back application components to the prior running version
Restore the control-plane database from the pre-upgrade snapshot (if migrations were applied)
estimated_restoration_time: Typically on the order of tens of minutes. Exact time is dependent on the snapshot mechanism (PITR vs volume snapshot) and database size.
support_commitment: We can staff planned maintenance windows with Redwood support and SRE escalation.
required_advance_notice: A minimum of 48 hours notice is required to schedule support engagement.
support_delivery: Live bridge will be opened at the start of the maintenance window.
Redwood SRE/release escalation is available continuously until completion or confirmed rollback.
additional_services: Rollback drills in non-production environments are available upon request.
audit_reporting: An upgrade report containing precheck results and timestamps for backup/upgrade steps is provided.
audit_log_availability: Audit log entries reflecting upgrade start/stop and rollback invocation are available, contingent on the specific version deployed.
